title: Geiger Counter Background Drift Watch
dataSources: Seismograph events (`seismograph:event`), seismic noise (`seismograph:noise`), air quality (`airquality:reading`), radiation counts (`radiation:count`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), phenology observations (`phenology:observation`), and weather-station rainfall (`weatherstation:reading`).
app: Citizen-science telemetry from seismographs, weather stations, air-quality monitors, Geiger counters, lightning feeds, and phenology journals streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=radiation:count
| timechart span=1d avg(cpm) as avg_cpm
| eventstats avg(avg_cpm) as baseline_cpm
| eval drift_pct=round(100*(avg_cpm-baseline_cpm)/baseline_cpm,1)
description: Measures how daily background radiation counts drift away from the longer-term baseline.
value: Radiation hobby data is mostly about consistency, and a drift watch helps you spot sensor issues or real environmental changes.
implementation: Ingest counts per minute from a Geiger counter and compare rolling daily averages against the historical norm.
visualization: Line chart of daily CPM with percent drift from baseline.
grandmaExplanation: It maps whether normal background radiation levels are staying steady or slowly changing in a way worth checking.
